newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli hawk Sharon demands high security post.
newsitem.headline: Israeli hawk Sharon demands high security post.

text.p: Israeli hawk Ariel Sharon, poised to become finance minister, demanded on Tuesday he also get a top security job for the first time since he was forced out as defence minister over a 1982 massacre of Palestinians.
Sharon's demand came as Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu grappled with strains in his ruling coalition hours before a parliamentary no-confidence vote and cabinet reshuffle.

Sharon, 69, insisted Netanyahu let him join Defence Minister Yitzhak Mordechai and Foreign Minister David Levy in making up the Israeli leader's team of insiders who hammer out strategy in Arab-Israeli negotiations.
"I stated (to Netanyahu) in a very clear fashion that I have to be on this team...that deals with political security issues," Sharon, of Netanyahu's Likud party, told Israel Radio.
Political analysts said the burly ex-general was sure to get the post -- a move likely to alarm the Arab world and the United States, Israel's closest ally.

Analysts said Levy and Mordechai, relative moderates in the rightist-religious government, were worried the appointment would yank the cabinet rightward at a time of rising tensions with the PLO over a three-month-old freeze in peace moves.

"This is something devastating for David Levy and Yitzhak Mordechai because they never wanted to share strategy and ideas with Sharon," Shimon Shiffer of the Yedioth Ahronoth newspaper said. "For the Americans and Palestinians, it's very scary."
Israeli markets were also jittery. Early trading in the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange was off 1.9 percent which analysts attributed mainly to Sharon's imminent appointment.

Five Likud lawmakers were expected to abstain or absent themselves from Tuesday's no-confidence vote in parliament. Five legislators from the Likud-allied Gesher faction headed by Levy were also expected to abstain.
But the opposition, despite ruling coalition defections, was seen as unlikely to muster the 61 votes required to force new elections for parliament and prime minister.
The vote was due to take place after 8:30 p.m. (1730 GMT).

Sharon was expected to take Dan Meridor's place in the cabinet reshuffle due to be announced on Tuesday. Meridor, Netanyahu's Likud rival, was forced out as finance minister last week in a struggle over currency reform.

The appointment marks a stunning political comeback since Sharon was forced to quit as defence minister in 1983 after a state inquiry found him indirectly responsible for the killing of hundreds of Palestinians by Lebanese Christian militiamen at two Beirut refugee camps encircled by Israeli troops.
"Sharon's the best player in town," Shiffer said. "He's taking Netanyahu to school."
The post would give Sharon wide-ranging powers to expand Jewish settlements in the Israeli-occupied West Bank and Gaza.
Sharon -- nicknamed "the bulldozer" -- as housing minister in the early 1990s engineered a settlement boom that put Israel on a collision course with the United States.
Netanyahu's embrace of Sharon was widely seen as a move to shore up the Likud's right wing while threatened with a party rebellion over Meridor's departure.

The Israeli leader's judgment has come into question on issues ranging from Jewish settlement expansion which has plunged Middle East peacemaking into crisis to a political appointment scandal from which he narrowly escaped indictment.

Tourism Minister Moshe Katzav was expected to be named Infrastructure Minister when Sharon was shifted to the Treasury. The tourism and science portfolios were expected to be filled respectively by Likud lawmakers Silvan Shalom and Michael Eitan.

Analysts said Sharon had masterfully exploited the political crisis to dramatically increase his power. Sharon said he had also requested some of his current authorities as infrastructure minister be carried over into the finance ministry.
